big: Central banks bought a net 289 tonnes of gold in Q2 2026, a record for a second quarter. Poland and China led the buying. Russia was the largest seller. Why do governments buy gold at all?

lines: Why would a central bank hold gold?
Gold is a reserve asset that is no one else's promise to pay. Central banks have been steady buyers. The World Gold Council expects that to continue, a little slower than the last four years.
